parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs national birth-sex document/entry rules and birth-sex facility bans with a state law covering airports and other public buildings, enforced by criminal/civil penalties and private bounty suits. A discrepancy can trigger refusal and, if wilfull misrepresentation is found, permanent fraud ineligibility; detention risks documented mistreatment and birth-sex placement. No execution or likely imprisonment is documented, and courts, legal aid, and state anti-discrimination law provide some recourse, but the facility and entry exposures are universal and the bounty removes reliance on prosecutors. Minors face the same facility rules and restricted care, with one care ban enjoined.

entry_documents.exposure: National policy limits passports to M/F per supporting documents; February 2025 cable requires refusal where documents/records discrepancy casts reasonable doubt on sex, and permanent lifetime ineligibility may be considered for wilful misrepresentation. Existing X passports remain valid.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic, with limited waivers. Civil-liberties suit challenges passport restrictions.
entry_documents.interaction: A passport/presentation discrepancy at entry can escalate from refusal to a fraud-based permanent bar, then to detention/facility placement by birth sex.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections adopted conversion-therapy-like policies including hair cutting and hormone removal; immigration custody reports include forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of transgender men. One bathroom arrest resulted in 24 hours in men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts have blocked or enjoined several national orders; habeas and other challenges are active, though outcomes vary and are unresolved.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry or facility enforcement can lead to custody where documented abuse and birth-sex placement increase severity beyond the initial fine/refusal.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State law confines transgender people to birth-sex facilities in publicly owned buildings including schools, universities, airports and government offices, with civil/criminal penalties up to $1,000 and bounty suits of at least $1,000 by private persons. Nationally, 9 states plus one unit ban this in all government buildings and 4 make some use criminal.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states, 4 units and the capital district have no mapped ban, but this division does. State anti-discrimination law since 2020 covers public accommodations generally, yet the specific facility law restricts bathrooms.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Private bounty enforcement means a visitor in an airport or public building faces exposure without any state prosecutor initiating action; the specific ban governs over general accommodation protection for restrooms.

care_services.exposure: National executive action targets gender-affirming care for minors; state minor-care ban was enacted in 2025, and hormone removal is documented in national custody. Visitor hormone continuity at public clinics is not_documented in this division.
care_services.protection: A state district judge granted a temporary injunction in May 2026 blocking enforcement of the minor-care ban in a parental lawsuit; several national orders have been blocked or enjoined.
care_services.interaction: Care restrictions affect a travelling minor and guardian more than an adult, while facility and document rules affect both regardless of care access.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive order defines sex as binary at birth, bars gender-identity facilities in government-funded spaces, and removes gender-identity materials; counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender. Four states make some facility use criminal in specified circumstances.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity since 2009; state hate-crime law does not, but national law remains available. Courts continue to hear challenges.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing and private bounty suits combine to encourage reporting and enforcement beyond police initiation.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor is subject to same birth-sex facility rules in schools and public buildings; state bans transgender girls from female school sports and restricts gender-affirming care for under-18s, subject to injunction. National order directs investigation/prosecution related to school social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Minor-care ban enforcement was temporarily enjoined in May 2026; parental litigation is active. No visitor-specific minor detention rule is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian cannot cure facility or document exposure for the minor; school, airport and clinic encounters each apply birth-sex rules independently.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented pattern of organised street sweeps, hate killings, or police extortion against transgender visitors is in the dossier. Public opinion cited supports assigned-sex documents and sports rules, indicating social friction/hostility risk but not measured violence prevalence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; state anti-discrimination law since 2020 and civil-liberties organisations provide reporting/legal support, though state hate-crime enhancements exclude gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Low documented street campaign does not offset universal facility/entry exposure; private bounty suits shift enforcement from police to members of the public.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Facility-law lawsuit filed within days is unresolved with no ruling recorded; bounty-suit volume, licence-notice numbers, and visitor enforcement data are not documented. Passport and executive-order challenges remain unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts, legal aid, anti-discrimination law, and examples of injunctions/blocked orders show remedies can work, but no documented remedy has yet overturned this division's facility/bounty law.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved litigation leaves the operative exposure in force during travel; a visitor on a short trip cannot rely on future invalidation.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in routine exclusion without imprisonment and weak effective remedy for the specific rule, but this case has stronger courts, active litigation and anti-discrimination law, and a possible permanent fraud bar rather than only denial/departure, so not materially below 0.35.

Higher severity than 0.55-B: instead of mainly secondary screening and discretionary refused admission, this regime adds universal birth-sex facility bans in airports with private bounty suits and documented custodial abuse if detained.

Higher than 0.25-C because there is no documented birth-sex prison system applied to visitors generally, no raids/extortion pattern, and imprisonment is not the typical outcome; documented custody abuse is serious but detention is not the routine pathway.

Close to 0.45-A: routine document-linked exposure, detention/humiliation and denial of services without likely custodial sentence or execution. The bounty mechanism and permanent-ineligibility risk pull this case somewhat below 0.45.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is document discrepancy or birth-sex facility use in an airport/public building leading to refusal, bounty/criminal penalty, possible fraud-based permanent ineligibility, and, if detained, documented mistreatment and birth-sex placement. General anti-discrimination and hate-crime protections and active courts mitigate street and employment risks but do not cancel the specific entry/facility rules, which are enforced by officers and private plaintiffs. That universal, unavoidable exposure with severe downstream risks places the combined regime in the elevated-risk range, above organised-targeting and imprisonment anchors and below administrative-friction anchors.
